messages.subject: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: I pulled together the open decisions from Atlas, the research circle, and Harbor operations. Please confirm which context should remain visible across relationship and project pages.

messages.subject: Re: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: The product context should preserve the decision, its source, and who changed the direction. Priya and Leah's synthesis notes are a useful model.

messages.subject: Re: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: For research context, keep the evidence boundary explicit and show where an interpretation came from. Leah can help make that readable without flattening uncertainty.

messages.subject: Re: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: For Harbor, the useful context is ownership and follow-through: who made the commitment, what participants were told, and whether the loop closed.

messages.subject: Re: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: I agree. Operational memory should retain the runbook decision, the named owner, and the validation step so the next event does not restart from scratch.

messages.subject: Re: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: I will draft a compact narrative pattern that separates sourced facts, interpretation, and unresolved questions while keeping the citations close to each claim.

messages.subject: Re: Cross-team memory review
messages.body: I incorporated the research, community, and editorial guidance. The next review will compare the relationship summaries against these source messages.
